name: Battle_AddCounterLoopAction
signature: BattleAct* Battle_AddCounterLoopAction(BattleActTable* table, BattleUnit* owner, unsigned int slot, const char* anim_name, int enabled)
summary: Adds one action entry to the battle action table: allocates 0x2C bytes from the table's own heap, runs the loop-action constructor on them, and installs the object in the requested slot; if the slot cannot be stored the fresh object is destroyed again. Used for the ten 'counter_loopNN' entries.
evidence: Sole caller 0x003744C8 (battle action table builder) passes this function exactly the ten 'counter_loop01'..'counter_loop10' strings with slots 0x81..0x8A; the function checks slot < table->f_40 (object count), allocates 0x2C with func_00109DC8(size, table->f_2c) and calls the loop-action constructor func_004A91CC, then func_002A8BA4(table, slot, obj) stores it; the constructor chain 0x4A91CC -> 0x38ACEC -> 0x193D84 stores the action name as an SSO string at +8 and the owner at +0x28, and the resulting vtable 0x00775D74 has a method 0x004A91AC that forwards this+8 (the animation name) to owner->vtable+0x84. Sibling functions 0x006D5D4C / 0x006D5DE8 / 0x006D5E84 have the identical body and are used for 'stskill/acskill', 'counter_act' and 'counter_end', i.e. only the action class differs.

name: Battle_AddSkillAction
signature: BattleAct* Battle_AddSkillAction(BattleActTable* table, BattleUnit* owner, unsigned int slot, const char* anim_name, int enabled)
summary: Same table insert as Battle_AddCounterLoopAction but constructs the skill-animation action class: allocates 0x2C bytes, builds the action object around the given animation name, stores it in the table slot and destroys it again if the slot write fails.
evidence: Called from 0x003744C8 for 'skill_01'..'skill_13' (slots 0x0F..0x16 and 0x6C..0x70) and 'cskill_01'..'cskill_16' (0x3C..0x45, 0x5A..0x5F); identical body to 0x006D5F20 except the constructor: func_004ED364, whose vtable 0x0077BE8C carries 0x004ED870 (drives owner->f_28->f_224 animations through func_0040A8C4) - i.e. this class plays an animation on the acting unit rather than looping a counter.

name: maybe_Ui_PanelStack_1Out_SetEntry
signature: void maybe_Ui_PanelStack_1Out_SetEntry(UiPane* self, const ResourceEntry* entry)
summary: Second entry of the class descriptor of a 3D UI pane: (re)builds the pane's mesh child from the given resource entry and then re-applies display mode 4. This variant returns the animation name 'g3101_1_out'.
evidence: Body is byte-identical to its four siblings 0x006E668C / 0x006E6724 / 0x006E67BC / 0x006E68EC: it calls 0x005F541C(self, entry), which allocates a 'mesh'-typed 3D node (type string 'mesh' at 0x005F550C, node created by 0x00225D90, placed by 0x00221AA8, attached by 0x005E7650) and stores it in self->f_160, then tail-calls self->vtable[0x40](self, 4). The class descriptor at 0x0076E2C8 has the deleting destructor 0x006E661C at [0], this function at [1], the shared UiWindow methods 0x005F7F98 / 0x005F8120 / ... and at slot +0x74 the accessor 0x0064D528, which simply returns the string 'g3101_1_out' (0x007C2ACE). That string is one of the animations baked into model g3101a (a 1x1 UI quad; its BCH holds g3101_1_in, g3101_1_out, g3101_2_in..g3101_5_in), so the five classes are the in/out stages of a 3D panel stack. Because the five bodies are identical, only the attached animation names distinguish them.

name: maybe_Ui_PanelStack_1In_SetEntry
signature: void maybe_Ui_PanelStack_1In_SetEntry(UiPane* self, const ResourceEntry* entry)
summary: Same mesh rebuild + display-mode-4 step as the other four panel-stage panes; this class is bound to the 'g3101_1_in' animation.
evidence: Identical body to 0x006E65F4 (calls 0x005F541C then vtable+0x40 with mode 4). Its class descriptor at 0x0076E380 keeps the destructor 0x006E66B4 and puts the shared UiWindow methods around it; slot +0x74 is 0x0064D534, a one-instruction accessor returning the literal 'g3101_1_in' (0x007C2ADA). That animation belongs to the 1x1 UI quad model g3101a (strings 'g3101_1_in'..'g3101_5_in' inside game_data/packs/3d/model/g3101a/g3101a.bch), matching the 'panel_3d_up_*' pane family in the layouts.

name: maybe_Ui_PanelStack_2In_SetEntry
signature: void maybe_Ui_PanelStack_2In_SetEntry(UiPane* self, const ResourceEntry* entry)
summary: Panel-stack stage pane bound to the 'g3101_2_in' animation: rebuilds the pane mesh from the entry and re-applies display mode 4.
evidence: Byte-identical to 0x006E65F4/0x006E668C (0x5F541C mesh rebuild then virtual slot 0x40 with the value 4). The class descriptor at 0x0076E438 has destructor 0x006E674C and its slot +0x74 is 0x0064D540, the accessor returning 'g3101_2_in' (0x007C2AE5); the animation name exists inside the g3101a UI quad model, so this is the second slide-in stage of the same panel stack.

name: maybe_Ui_PanelStack_3In_SetEntry
signature: void maybe_Ui_PanelStack_3In_SetEntry(UiPane* self, const ResourceEntry* entry)
summary: Panel-stack stage pane bound to the 'g3101_3_in' animation: rebuilds the pane mesh from the entry and re-applies display mode 4.
evidence: Byte-identical body to the sibling panel panes (0x005F541C mesh rebuild, then vtable+0x40(self, 4)). Class descriptor at 0x0076E4F0, destructor 0x006E67E4, slot +0x74 = 0x0064D54C returning 'g3101_3_in' (0x007C2AF0), an animation of the g3101a UI quad.

name: maybe_Ui_PanelStack_5In_SetEntry
signature: void maybe_Ui_PanelStack_5In_SetEntry(UiPane* self, const ResourceEntry* entry)
summary: Panel-stack stage pane bound to the 'g3101_5_in' animation: rebuilds the pane mesh from the entry and re-applies display mode 4.
evidence: Same code as 0x006E65F4..0x006E67BC (0x005F541C then virtual slot 0x40 with mode 4). Class descriptor 0x0076E660, destructor 0x006E6914, slot +0x74 = 0x0064D564 returning 'g3101_5_in' (0x007C2B06). The missing 'g3101_4_in' pane is its own class (accessor 0x0064D558) outside this batch.

name: Ui_CasinoSlotQueen_Init
signature: void Ui_CasinoSlotQueen_Init(UiWindow* self, void* owner, int group, int layer, int flags)
summary: Initialiser of the casino-slot window that plays the 'queen' effect: runs the shared UiWindow base init, then creates the window's animation/layout object from the resource name 'queen' and stores it in self->f_4c.
evidence: Calls the shared UiWindow initialiser 0x001A6520 (hundreds of callers across the UI code) and forwards the caller's stack argument to it; then func_0053D604(self->f_4, name_id, 0, 1, stackarg) with the id from func_0065424C, a two-instruction accessor whose inline literal is 'queen' (0x00654254). 0x0053D604 builds an animation player (0x51D03C resolves the resource, 0x535D3C parses it, 0x5402F0 object with vtable 0x0053D714, 0x536424 binds element 0 of the 0x24-byte entry table); the result is kept at +0x4C. 'queen' is exactly the animation of layout menu_slot_queen_3d (game_assets/layouts/..menu_slot_queen_3d_queen.bflan.json) and there are queen_chara/queen_effect1..5 textures in casino_slot_3d. The class descriptor at 0x00779B50 keeps the deleting destructor 0x006E7260 and the shared UiWindow slots 0x00291220/0x001A6460.

name: Ui_CasinoSlotFreeSpin_Init
signature: void Ui_CasinoSlotFreeSpin_Init(UiWindow* self, void* owner, int group, int layer, int flags)
summary: Initialiser of the casino-slot free-spin window: shared UiWindow base init, then creates and stores the animation player for the resource name 'freespin' in self->f_4c.
evidence: Identical shape to 0x006E7220; the only difference is the name accessor func_0065425C, whose inline literal is 'freespin' (bytes at 0x00654264: 'free' 'spin'). Layout menu_slot_freespin_3d with animation menu_slot_freespin_3d_freespin.bflan exists, and the belt layout menu_slot_belt_freespin_n_3d carries the free-spin symbol. Class descriptor at 0x00779BB8, destructor 0x006E72B0.

name: Ui_CasinoSlotMetalChange_Init
signature: void Ui_CasinoSlotMetalChange_Init(UiWindow* self, void* owner, int group, int layer, int flags)
summary: Initialiser of the casino-slot metal-change window: shared UiWindow base init, then creates and stores the animation player for the resource name 'metalchange' in self->f_4c.
evidence: Same code as 0x006E7220/0x006E7270; name accessor func_00654270 returns the literal 'metalchange' (0x00654278). Layout menu_slot_metalchange_3d + animation menu_slot_metalchange_3d_metalchange.bflan exist, and menu_slot_belt_metalchange_n_3d is the matching belt symbol; class descriptor at 0x00779C1C, destructor 0x006E7300.

name: Container_NameHashFind
signature: void Container_NameHashFind(HashIterPair* out, NameHashMap* map, const NameHashKey* key)
summary: Looks a (string-hash, string) key up in the engine's name hash map and returns an iterator pair (found node, insertion hint). Descends the ordered tree by the 32-bit hash, then walks equal-hash neighbours verifying the name with strcmp, so hash collisions stay correct.
evidence: The key is exactly the 8-byte struct built by Container_StringHashMapInsert (0x001E88E4): {u32 hash; const char* name}. The code reads map->f_8 as root, tests the colour byte at node+0x10, compares node->f_14 (hash) and uses func_0010540C (newlib-style word-at-a-time strcmp, verified in asm at 0x0010540C) on node->f_18 (name); tree steps go through func_00115358 / 0x00115390 (rb-tree increment/decrement) and the result pair {node, hint-parent} is what 0x001E88E4 compares against the end sentinel. Callers: 0x001E88E4 (string hash map insert). Companion instantiations: 0x6F333C (same map with an embedded base) and 0x6F359C (insert).

name: maybe_Container_NameHashFindEmbedded
signature: void maybe_Container_NameHashFindEmbedded(HashIterPair* out, NameHashMap* map, const NameHashKey* key)
summary: Second instantiation of the name hash map lookup for a map whose payload node embeds its key/value at +0x10; returns the same (node, insertion hint) pair as Container_NameHashFind.
evidence: The descent and the hash/name comparison are identical to 0x006F322C, but every key/name read is routed through `base = node + 0x10` (Ghidra renders it as `iVar4 = *piVar2; if (iVar4) iVar4 += 0x10`), and the function is the only other user of the same rb-tree helpers 0x00115358/0x00115390. Caller 0x0056F3F8 passes a field inside an object, i.e. a map embedded in a larger class. Exact map owner not established.

name: Container_NameHashInsert
signature: NameHashNode* Container_NameHashInsert(NameHashMap* map, NameHashNode* node, unsigned int hash)
summary: Inserts a pre-built hash node into the name hash map: walks down by the 32-bit hash, decides left/right insertion, rebalances the red-black tree and writes the hash into the node; returns the inserted node.
evidence: Descends comparing node->f_14 with the hash argument (func_0011FFC4), stores arg3 in node->f_14, links it with func_0010EE9C (rb-tree link, colour at +0x10) and rebalances through func_0010EC00/func_0010EC14; the map header fields map->f_c / map->f_8 are the rb-tree leftmost/header of 0x006F322C. Caller 0x005F6E50 inserts UI data nodes into a map embedded at self->f_1ec. The node layout (self-linked links, colour byte at +0x10, hash at +0x14, name at +0x18) matches what Container_StringHashMapInsert (0x001E88E4) allocates.

name: maybe_Str_InsertAt
signature: void* maybe_Str_InsertAt(void* dst, unsigned int pos, const char* text, unsigned int max_chars)
summary: Inserts text into a small-string object at byte offset pos: saves the tail from pos, truncates the string there, appends text (bounded by max_chars and the 32-byte inline capacity) and then re-appends the saved tail; pos past the end degenerates to a plain append. Returns dst.
evidence: dst is the engine's small-string layout (data at +4, inline capacity 0x1F/0x20 - the same 0x1F threshold used in 0x005F541C and 0x003744C8): strlen(dst+4), strlen(dst+pos+4), a 0x1F-capped copy of the tail, `dst[pos]=0`, then func_00100990 - verified in asm/readable to be strncat (it seeks the terminator, then copies src for at most n bytes) - for text and again for the tail. Callers 0x00220F78 / 0x002232FC / 0x00224394 are UI text builders that prepend/insert a name at offset 0 into a locally built string; arg4 is passed as 1 there, which is why it reads as a length cap. The exact public API it belongs to (std::string::insert-like helper vs. a local path builder) is not proven.

name: maybe_Container_HandleResolveAsType
summary: Resolves a handle through the engine's global object table and returns the object of the expected runtime type (the type id this function is specialised for), or null. The table maps handle pages to lists of objects; the runtime type is checked by calling the object's virtual type query.
evidence: Same table idiom as the rest of the object registry: page compare against g_007134F4 (0x000FFFFF) and bucket array g_007134F8 (=0x007BA2D0), then it walks the object list at entry+0x7C and accepts the element whose virtual slot 0 returns g_007134FC (the registered type id for this wrapper). Callers 0x0030A0E0, 0x004A7E58, 0x0061BEBC, 0x001F21CC etc. use it to turn an embedded handle (e.g. self->f_13c) into the live resource object. N_006 already documented the same registry idiom for 0x004C459C (type-4 objects), which calls this function.

name: maybe_Container_HandleResolveAsTypeByName
signature: void* maybe_Container_HandleResolveAsTypeByName(const Handle* handle, const char* name)
summary: Like Container_HandleResolveAsType but additionally requires the object's 64-byte name field to equal the given name, so a handle that fans out to several objects can be resolved to the named one (e.g. one '*.packinfo.epi' inside a handle).
evidence: Identical registry walk (mask g_00713850, table g_00713854 = 0x007BA2D0, type id g_00713858), but before the type test it copies the object's 16 words at +0x14..+0x50 (= a 0x40-byte inline name) and compares them with arg2 via func_00123660(.., 0x40), i.e. memcmp. Callers pass pack-info file names: 0x0035F9F8 ('effect_packinfo.epi'), 0x003DBE60 / 0x003DBFC8 ('effect2d_packinfo.epi'), and the returned object exposes f_90->f_60/f_6c/f_78 name arrays plus f_84 count - a pack index used by Container_BuildStringMap (0x001E8BCC) to build a name map.

name: std_introsort_loop
signature: void std_introsort_loop(SortRecord* first, SortRecord* last, int depth_limit)
summary: Introsort core of the C++ std::sort used on 8-byte (u32 id, float weight) records: median-of-three quicksort partitioning with ascending float comparison, recursion on the right half, and a heapsort fallback once the depth budget is exhausted so the worst case stays O(n log n).
evidence: Standard libstdc++ introsort shape: `while (last-first > 0x80 bytes)` = 16 elements, median-of-three pivot on the float at +4, Hoare partition, `depth_limit /= 2` plus a recursive call on the cut and a loop on the left part, and on exhaustion a make-heap + sort-heap pass (the classic call to __partial_sort). Caller 0x0028BCB0 wraps it exactly like std::__sort: calls this function, then 0x00717F88 (final insertion sort) and its own second stage 0x00717F88/0x00717F88-style pass, on an array of 8-byte records whose weight is at +4. No strings, no globals - pure template code, so no subsystem prefix.
